note: The interior of a BPMN file, as its own subgraph. Separate from the DAK component layer because the vocabulary here is OMG's rather than WHO's, the extractor reads XML rather than FSH, and the failure modes are different: a DAK component is wrong when it points at a file that does not exist, a BPMN subgraph is wrong when it misreads the file it did find. The edge that joins the two -- `business-process sourcedFrom bpmn-definitions` -- is declared HERE rather than in l2, because l2 must not import this layer (l2-bpmn already imports l2 for persona, and the reverse would be circular). Declaring an edge in the layer that can see both ends is the same thing `dak-task describes bpmn-task` does.

groundedIn.detail: 8 participants, 8 processes, 61 tasks, 1 sub-process, 3 exclusive gateways, 8 start and 8 end events, 70 sequence flows (6 of them named, 0 with a conditionExpression), 10 message flows, 0 lanes. The classes below are the element types this file actually contains, not BPMN 2.0's full element set.

groundedIn.what: The DAK-level task list that duplicates part of it
groundedIn.detail: `task 0..*` with identifier, name and description -- the same tasks the BPMN draws, listed again in FSH. `describes` joins the two so they can be checked against each other; today nothing does.

A pool's @name matches an ActorDefinition's `title`, not its `name`. Committed instances title two of the eight pools differently from the pool that names them, so the join fails on real data and nothing reports it.

valueSets.note: BPMN 2.0's gatewayDirection. Added by the smart-base migration: smart-kg named the property without binding it.

codes.definition: No constraint on incoming and outgoing flows.
Many incoming flows, at most one outgoing.
At most one incoming flow, many outgoing.
Many incoming and many outgoing flows.

predicates.note: A sequence flow, within one process. The qualifier carries the flow's name where it has one -- 6 of 70 in the lifecycle BPMN, all gateway branches such as "Yes - approved". No flow in that file carries a conditionExpression, so the label is the whole of the branch condition and nothing more is claimed. `openQualifier` says the value is free text authored in the diagram, not a term from a vocabulary, so an unseen label is not a finding.

A message flow, which by definition crosses participants. Kept distinct from flowsTo because a handoff between two roles is what governance and country adaptation look for, and burying 10 of them among 70 intra-process flows loses them.

A participant pool is performed by a persona. STRING EQUALITY between the pool's @name and an ActorDefinition's title, across two file formats with no shared identifier. Compare l2:fulfilledBy, where a requirement names a persona by Canonical() and resolves without guessing -- the mechanism exists; BPMN does not use it. Every instance carries a resolutionStatus.

classes.name: BPMN File
classes.note: One BPMN file as a unit -- the `bpmn:definitions` root. Shares its IRI with the l1:external-artifact for the same file, so the component that points at it and the subgraph that opens it name one resource.

classes.name: BPMN Process
classes.note: One `bpmn:process`. Present as a node because a participant references it by processRef, and without it the pool-to-element attribution has nothing to travel through.

classes.name: BPMN Participant
classes.note: A pool: a role that owns part of the collaboration. The lifecycle BPMN has 8 and declares no laneSet at all, so the pool is the only unit of role assignment present and its @name is the sole link to a persona.

classes.name: BPMN Task
classes.note: A task or sub-process. It is what a DMN usingTask href points at, what sequence flows connect, and what a DAK-level task entry describes. Sub-processes carry isSubProcess rather than getting a class of their own -- the lifecycle BPMN has exactly one.

classes.name: BPMN Gateway
classes.note: A branch or merge. Included for connectivity rather than for a cross-model edge: a flow through a gateway with no node would point at nothing, and every reachability question over the process would break at the first decision point.

classes.name: BPMN Event
classes.note: A start or end event. Same connectivity argument as gateway, plus one of its own: entry and exit points are what make 'is this task reachable' and 'does this path terminate' answerable at all.

deliberatelyOmitted.why: The class would have no instance: the lifecycle BPMN uses pools only and declares no laneSet. Add it when a DAK ships one.
70 sequence flows, 0 conditionExpression elements. The branch label carries all there is, so it is the flowsTo qualifier and nothing more is claimed.
Presentation. Coordinates answer no question this graph exists to answer, and the layout lives in a separate .layout.bpmn file anyway.
